title: dedicated: autoscaler burst & throughput reporting enhancement
author: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Improve Dedicated autoscaler reporting for burst capacity and end-to-end throughput guarantees. Motivation: customers running bursty inference workloads (short windows of high QPS) need clearer telemetry and SLO-aligned reporting to understand how burst capacity is consumed and whether throughput guarantees were met. Design: add new per-fleet burst_token_bucket metrics, introduce a dedicated 'burst_throughput' reporting pipeline that correlates tokenbucket state with actual served throughput, and surface a utilization breakdown in the Console. Changes include instrumentation in the autoscaler, a reporting worker that aggregates 1s/10s windows, Grafana dashboards and a small API extension to expose historical burst consumption for rollouts and billing reconciliation. Checklist: - [x] Add tokenbucket metrics and events from autoscaler - [x] Emit per-fleet throughput samples with burst attribution - [x] New reporting pipeline + DB schema migration script - [x] Console panels and Dashboard JSON - [x] Unit + integration + load tests - [x] Docs and release notes Notes: kept changes backward-compatible with existing utilization metrics; new metrics are opt-in for fleets that enable 'burst_reporting: true' to avoid extra cardinality.

Diego Ramos: Approve after nits fixed

load test (burst_sim): pass (sustained 3x baseline for 2m windows)
release_notes:
- Add opt-in burst reporting for Dedicated fleets (burst_reporting flag)
- New per-fleet burst_throughput metrics and Grafana dashboard
- API: /v1/dedicated/fleets/{id}/burst-reporting for historical burst consumption
- Improved autoscaler instrumentation for throughput guarantee troubleshooting
change_summary: Introduces opt-in burst reporting and a reporting pipeline that correlates tokenbucket state with served throughput to improve visibility into burst consumption and throughput guarantees.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for tokenbucket and CAS refills; integration tests validate reporting pipeline end-to-end; e2e scenario simulates bursty traffic and verifies console panels; load tests validate sustained bursts at 3x baseline for 2-minute windows with no regressions in latency SLOs.
motivation: Customers were unable to reconcile dedicated fleet billing and SLO breaches during short, high-QPS bursts because token consumption and actual served throughput were reported separately. This PR unifies those signals to make root-cause analysis and capacity planning easier.
risk_notes: Risk: increased metric cardinality and DB write volume. Mitigations: opt-in flag, aggregation (1s/10s) to limit resolution, DB migration adds retention TTL, Canary rollout to 10% of fleets for 48h before full rollout.
migration_instructions: Run internal/store/migrations/20260220_add_burst_reporting.sql against the reporting DB. Migration is backward-compatible; new tables are ignored by older services.
notes_for_release_engineering: Schedule a 48h canary rollout with 'burst_reporting: true' enabled for a subset of fleets. Coordinate with billing to validate historical reconciliations for sample fleets.
estimated_impact: Improves debugging time for burst SLO incidents by ~40% (internal estimate) and enables customers to see exact burst consumption used against throughput guarantees.
human_readable_summary: Merged enhancement: opt-in burst reporting for Dedicated fleets, new metrics and dashboards, API for historical burst consumption, and several tests and docs updates. Backward-compatible and gated via feature flag.
